item.title: AI to take center stage at 5th global digital expo
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-08
BEIJING, Sept. 8 (Xinhua) -- The 5th Global Digital Trade Expo, an event dedicated to promoting digital trade and industrial cooperation, will take place from Sept. 23 to 27 in Hangzhou, capital of east China's Zhejiang Province, with artificial intelligence (AI) as its main theme, an official said on Monday. More than one-third of the exhibitors will focus on AI, alongside the collective debut of AI application pilot bases, presenting a full-chain innovation ecosystem spanning foundational models, industry applications and smart devices, China's Vice Minister of Commerce Yan Dong noted. A number of AI competitions will be held on the sidelines of the expo, covering areas such as open-source development, embodied intelligence and brain-computer interface technology. The expo will feature 170,000 square meters of exhibition space, with international exhibitors accounting for over 20 percent of the total. The number of overseas pavilions has already exceeded the combined total of all previous editions. Malaysia and Hungary will be the guest countries of honor, while representatives from 121 countries and regions and 29 international organizations have confirmed their attendance. The expo has so far attracted nearly 40,000 professional buyers, including more than 12,000 from overseas, with expected international procurement orders reaching 977 million U.S. dollars. China's digitally deliverable service trade value expanded at an average annual rate of 11.2 percent between 2016 and 2025, outpacing the global average by 1.8 percentage points. According to a guideline on boosting reform and innovative development of digital trade released in November 2024, China expects the share of digitally deliverable service trade in total service trade to exceed 45 percent by 2029 and 50 percent by 2035. The Ministry of Commerce will work with other government departments to implement the guideline, support local governments in tailoring policies to boost digital trade, and foster a coordinated effort to advance the sector, Yan added. ■

item.title: Chinese stories find new ways to reach global audiences through immersive technology
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-08
VENICE, Italy, Sept. 8 (Xinhua) -- At a screening venue on a small island near Venice's Lido in Italy, a foreign visitor put on a virtual reality headset and stepped into a Chinese story. Outside the screening room, more viewers waited in line for their turn to experience The Pigeon Ring, a Chinese immersive work that explores family, memory and the bonds between generations. The scene at the 83rd Venice International Film Festival is a vivid example of how immersive storytelling is opening up new possibilities for Chinese creators to reach audiences around the world. Established in 2016, the Venice Immersive section is an official section of the festival and has grown into one of the world's largest events dedicated to immersive arts and media. It showcases creative extended reality (XR) works ranging from immersive videos and virtual and mixed reality experiences to virtual worlds and immersive installations. The Pigeon Ring, directed by Zhang Yuqi and Tao Shixin, has been selected for the Venice Immersive competition this year. It tells a story of a granddaughter who accompanies her grandfather back to their old family home in search of a lost pigeon ring. What begins as a seemingly ordinary family journey gradually unfolds into a story of memory, companionship and affection. "Most of the audiences who have come to see the work over the past few days have been from overseas," Zhang and Tao told Xinhua. "Many foreign viewers shed tears after watching it. Perhaps the work has touched something that people can emotionally relate to." That emotional connection across cultural boundaries has also left a deep impression on Michel Reilhac, co-curator of Venice Immersive. He described the work as "very moving," noting that without featuring broad narratives and spectacular visual scenes, The Pigeon Ring focuses on a much smaller story -- an ordinary family story -- yet manages to generate a powerful emotional impact. "It's not relying on special effects, but on the heart of the story itself," Reilhac told Xinhua, adding that this makes Chinese works accessible to and appreciated by international audiences. Behind these stories and emotional experiences lies another important force: rapidly evolving technology. Liz Rosenthal, co-curator of Venice Immersive, highlighted the use of Gaussian splatting, an advanced 3D rendering technique, in The Pigeon Ring, describing it as a particularly innovative approach. "It really takes you into the story in a way that we haven't seen before," she said. "It's almost like stepping into a film." "China has made incredible progress in artificial intelligence, robotics and all kinds of digital technologies," said Reilhac, adding that the country's technological development is moving in a highly forward-looking direction and is helping creators produce increasingly sophisticated immersive works. The co-curator also commended the development of talent training at Chinese universities. Recalling a recent visit to Shanghai Theatre Academy, Reilhac said he was impressed by the openness of young Chinese creators and artists toward international collaboration. He noted that, alongside The Pigeon Ring, a number of works by young Chinese artists are being presented at the festival's immersive section, with some creators still studying at university. "It's very important for us that we represent new voices, new artists alongside the more established ones," he said.■

item.title: Interview: China's services fair opens new doors in the "marketplace of ideas," says economist
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-08
JOHANNESBURG, Sept. 8 (Xinhua) -- China International Fair for Trade in Services (CIFTIS) is an important platform for economies and businesses to explore new opportunities in the services trade as knowledge and data become increasingly important drivers of global growth, a South African economist has said. "CIFTIS will increasingly move beyond being simply an exhibition and become a marketplace for ideas, technology, investment and international partnerships," Simphiwe Madikizela, professor of economics at the University of South Africa, told Xinhua in a recent interview. The 2026 CIFTIS will be held from Sept. 9 to 13 in Beijing, bringing together exhibitors from over 90 countries and international organizations, along with more than 1,800 companies. Madikizela said the fair's theme, "Global Services, Shared Prosperity," is particularly relevant as the global economy shifts from a model dominated by trade in manufacturing goods toward one increasingly driven by services, technology and intellectual property. China's rapidly growing services trade provides an important example of this transformation, he said, citing data that China's trade in services increased by 8.3 percent year-on-year to nearly 3.78 trillion yuan (about 556.56 billion U.S. dollars) in the first half of 2026. "China's services trade is increasingly moving toward higher-value activities," said Madikizela, noting that knowledge-intensive services trade reached 1.66 trillion yuan, accounting for 44 percent of total services trade, and grew 6.7 percent in the first half of the year, while exports of such services rose 12.8 percent. Such development is significant not only for China but also for the global economy, as the world's second-largest economy is becoming not only a major producer of goods but also an increasingly important market and provider of services, he added. Highlighting China's vast domestic market and demand, the economist said, "An open Chinese economy can support global growth through trade, investment, tourism, digital services, professional services, technology and innovation." "At a time when geopolitical tensions and protectionism are creating uncertainty, greater cooperation in services can provide another channel through which economies remain connected," Madikizela said, adding that against this backdrop, CIFTIS can play an important role in strengthening international services cooperation. CIFTIS reflects a broader transformation in globalization since international economic integration is no longer simply about moving physical products across borders, but increasingly about the exchange of knowledge, technology, skills, data and services, he said. Madikizela added that the development of China's services trade is contributing to what he described as the "servicification of global trade," as manufacturing and services become increasingly integrated. For developing economies, particularly in Africa, CIFTIS offers opportunities to connect with Chinese and international partners in areas such as digital trade, e-commerce, financial services, tourism, education, healthcare, logistics and professional services, he said. "The future will not be defined only by how many containers cross international borders but by how effectively countries exchange services, technology, knowledge, data, skills and innovation," Madikizela said. "That is why initiatives such as CIFTIS are becoming increasingly important to the global economy."■

item.title: China to reinvent centuries-old industries with heritage and AI
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-08
BEIJING, Sept. 7 (Xinhua) -- China on Monday unveiled its first national policy document for silk, tea, porcelain and other centuries-old industries, as part of efforts to leverage the country's rich cultural heritage and build strong global brands. By 2028, the country aims to cultivate 50 enterprises with annual revenues exceeding 10 billion yuan (about 1.48 billion U.S. dollars) each, Xie Yuansheng, vice minister of the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (MIIT), told a news conference. The document also calls for 100 Chinese consumer brands and several industrial clusters with annual output exceeding 100 billion yuan to be developed by 2028, he added. By 2030, these industries are expected to produce a group of world-class enterprises and renowned brands, while moving toward the mid- to high-end of the global value chain, according to the document issued by the MIIT and five other government departments. In addition to the industries mentioned above, the document also covers traditional Chinese medicine, brewing, arts and crafts, and the "four treasures of the study" -- writing brush, ink stick, paper and inkstone -- all deeply rooted in Chinese culture and traditions dating back centuries or even millennia. Representative sectors of these traditional industries boast about 25,000 enterprises above the designated size, employing nearly 3.5 million people and generating about 8 trillion yuan in annual revenue, according to Xie. Historically, these products traveled along ancient trade routes as far as Central Asia, the Mediterranean and even Africa, carrying Chinese craftsmanship and culture far beyond the country's borders. In recent years, the appeal of Chinese culture overseas has continued to rise. Content creators around the world are making aspects of Chinese culture part of their daily lives -- from drinking hot water and wearing slippers around the house to eating Chinese food and wearing red. The document also comes as China seeks to translate its rich cultural heritage into greater market competitiveness. About 90 percent of China's silk products are exported, but mainly as raw materials or original equipment manufacturer goods, with domestic brands having limited pricing power in the global market, said Feng Haicang, an official with the MIIT's consumer goods industry department. "Our challenge is to make sure these time-honored crafts are not only admired but also commercially successful, and to restore these historic Chinese products to their rightful place at the high end of international markets," said Feng. China will hold the first national exposition of time-honored industries in east China's Hangzhou City in late October, Xie said. AI is expected to play an important part in boosting these industries, according to the document. The technology will be used to digitize traditional craft knowledge, decode traditional production processes and improve efficiency and product quality on factory floors. In silk weaving, AI-assisted design can now generate thousands of patterns in minutes, said Xie. A DEEP POOL OF CRAFT KNOWLEDGE These industries draw strength from China's vast intangible cultural heritage, which provides a deep reservoir of craft knowledge, skills and cultural creativity for their continued development, said Shan Gangxin, an official with the Ministry of Culture and Tourism, at the news conference. Traditional arts, crafts and medicine, Shan noted, share deep roots with industries like silk, tea and porcelain, and have evolved alongside them. China now has 45 elements inscribed on UNESCO's lists and register of intangible cultural heritage, including silk craftsmanship, acupuncture and tea-processing techniques. More than 100,000 items are also recognized on national, provincial, prefectural and county-level intangible cultural heritage lists. In July, the Jingdezhen Handicraft Porcelain Industry Sites were added to the UNESCO World Heritage List. The country's large pool of skilled practitioners is also a solid base for industrial development. More than 200 universities have taken part in training programs for intangible cultural heritage practitioners over the past decade, benefiting more than 200,000 heritage inheritors, said Shan. The economic potential of traditional skills is already clear in the way they have been adapted to today's markets. Willow weaving in Linyi, east China's Shandong Province, for example, has evolved from a craft once best known for making baskets and hampers into a wide range of contemporary products, from stylish cultural and creative products to playful items such as cat climbing frames. The industry now has more than 300 patents and over 20,000 product designs, with its products reaching more than 80 countries and regions, according to Shan. Traditional craftsmanship is also finding new channels and audiences. This summer, creative products featuring hemp weaving, Huzhou writing brushes and Zhuang brocade were officially licensed for the 2026 FIFA World Cup. By the end of 2025, China had 14,900 intangible cultural heritage workshops, supporting employment and higher incomes for more than 1.3 million people, Shan said. ■

item.title: AI-powered "Made in China" sharpens global appeal in tech hub
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-08
SHENZHEN, Sept. 8 (Xinhua) -- Inside a flagship store of Chinese drone maker DJI in the city of Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, British visitor Annabel Grainger was busy taking photos of products to share with her friends back home. "My friends wouldn't have seen anything like that before," she said. A thriving tech hub, Shenzhen has emerged as a magnet for global tech aficionados. The city's wide range of high-tech products, including artificial intelligence (AI) glasses, AI 3D printers, AI robots, drones, and handheld gimbal cameras, have generated considerable buzz on international social media platforms such as Instagram and TikTok. An average of nearly 8,000 foreign buyers visit Huaqiangbei, Shenzhen's mega electronics marketplace, each day this year. From January through July, sales of AI products surged more than 55 percent from a year earlier in this area. Sales of AI glasses doubled, while sales of drones and robots climbed by 60 to 70 percent during the same period. Industry insiders noted that a complete industrial chain and high-density industrial clusters have taken shape in Huaqiangbei's AI sector, covering the full spectrum from AI chip solutions and agent development to on-device model deployment and scenario testing. These advantages, they said, have facilitated the deep integration of AI technologies into hardware products, while boosting production efficiency and significantly lowering costs. "It takes several weeks to make a prototype in Europe, but it can be done in half a day in Shenzhen," Dutch engineer Henk Werner said. "In Shenzhen, if you need to upgrade a product, you can pull together all your suppliers within a day and have a cooperation agreement inked by the evening," said Leng Xiaokun, founder of Leju Robotics, highlighting the city's core advantage in having a complete industrial chain. The company's Kuafu line of humanoid robots has, notably, achieved a domestic sourcing rate of 95 percent for its core components, which has significantly reduced costs and enabled rapid market launch. In a bid to incentivize enterprises to double down on fundamental core technologies over the long haul, Nanshan District in the city, home to a vibrant tech ecosystem, has set up a seed fund and an angel fund totaling 500 million yuan (approximately 73.7 million U.S. dollars), aimed at offering lead investment support to early-stage ventures. "Though the research and development of the fundamental components and algorithms of humanoid robots often yields no direct returns for several years, Shenzhen's patient capital provides a guarantee for technological breakthroughs," Leng noted. Leveraging an international cooperation center based in the city's Longhua District, a host of advanced technology firms have successfully introduced their AI-powered intelligent computing terminals and other smart products and solutions to markets across North America and Southeast Asia. Shenzhen has also jointly built cooperation platforms with ASEAN member states. The Shenzhen-Singapore cross-border data verification platform, now in trial operation, is designed to address challenges related to secure data flows in AI and other industries. Adjacent to Hong Kong, Shenzhen was one of China's first special economic zones and has since evolved, over four decades, into a global hub for innovation and advanced manufacturing. The number of AI enterprises in China had surpassed 6,000 last year, while the output value of the core AI industry was projected to exceed 1.2 trillion yuan during the same period, representing a year-on-year increase of almost 30 percent. Moreover, China was home to more than 140 humanoid robot developers in 2025, with shipments reaching 14,400 units -- accounting for 84.7 percent of the global market, an industry research report said. ■

item.title: Exploring new paths for sustainable development in Asia-Pacific
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-08
SHENZHEN, Sept. 8 (Xinhua) -- As the Asia-Pacific embraces a more digital, intelligent and green future, Chinese modernization is creating fresh opportunities for the region and beyond, said participants at the Asia-Pacific Media Forum. As an important part of the APEC "China Year" events, the forum, held on Saturday in the southern city of Shenzhen, brought together more than 400 representatives from over 40 countries and regions, as well as participants from the United Nations and other international organizations. They expressed hope that the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting, to be held in Shenzhen this November, will give fresh impetus to the building of an Asia-Pacific community, deepen regional cooperation and promote shared prosperity. ASIA-PACIFIC COMMUNITY As the host of APEC 2026, China has set "Building an Asia-Pacific Community to Prosper Together" as the theme of this year's event. "The Asia-Pacific Community is a partnership built on mutual respect, peaceful coexistence, shared prosperity, and cultural diversity. It is not merely a geographical concept but a community connected by common aspirations for stability, economic development, and human progress," said Saeed Ahmad, director-general of Pakistan Broadcasting Corporation. Home to one-third of the planet's population, the Asia-Pacific accounts for over 60 percent of global economic output and nearly half of global trade, making it a key driver of global economic growth. Kamphol Mahanukul, president of the Thai-Chinese Journalists Association, said that the Asia-Pacific miracle was not a historical coincidence, but was forged through a collective commitment to openness, practical cooperation and mutual respect. "The rise of Asia is a beautiful thing. It is helping provide a dynamic motor not just for the Asia-Pacific but for the global economy," said Sourabh Gupta, resident senior fellow at the Institute for China-America Studies. "The path to shared prosperity in the Asia-Pacific runs through cooperation, not coercion; through open trade, not walls; through dialogue, not division," said Shezra Mansab Ali Khan Kharal, Pakistan's minister of state for climate change and environmental coordination. OPENNESS, INNOVATION, COOPERATION Openness, innovation and cooperation are the three pillars of the APEC "China Year". Participants said they reflect the priorities of APEC economies and could, with greater emphasis, give a further boost to regional innovation and economic integration. "A prosperous and stable Asia-Pacific requires economies to preserve channels for trade, investment and dialogue even when external conditions become more difficult. An open and interconnected region also gives businesses more options to diversify markets, suppliers and logistics networks," said Nguyen Ha Phuong, principal researcher at the Institute for Asia-Pacific Studies under the Vietnam Academy of Social Sciences. You Sang Chul, head of the China Institute of the Korea JoongAng Daily, said Shenzhen had demonstrated how emerging technologies had become part of everyday life, citing autonomous vehicles and drone delivery services as examples. He noted that China was leading global innovation in areas such as AI while integrating digital and green technologies into its modernization drive, providing valuable experience and new opportunities for other Asia-Pacific economies. As the APEC "China year" has gathered momentum, member economies have stepped up practical cooperation in areas such as food security, fisheries and marine affairs, and energy. Felipe Cuadra, general counsel of Chile's daily La Tercera, said that Asia-Pacific cooperation had opened up broad new opportunities for Chile and that Latin America needs diverse and reliable partners to better withstand external shocks. CHINESE MODERNIZATION, NEW OPPORTUNITIES The APEC "China Year" coincides with the first year of China's 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030). At this new historical juncture, China is deepening reforms and pursuing higher-standard opening-up, creating new opportunities for the Asia-Pacific and beyond through its modernization. After touring the Hong Kong-Zhuhai-Macao Bridge, Felix Paz Quiroz, general director of the Peruvian news agency Andina, described the cross-sea link as an engineering marvel. He said the visit reminded him of Peru's Chancay Port, another major transportation hub, voicing the hope of drawing on China's experience to develop the port into an important gateway connecting Latin America and Asia. In recent years, China has shared the benefits of its institutional reforms with the rest of the world. From expanding its pilot free trade zones and advancing the Hainan Free Trade Port in the south to further opening its education, finance, and healthcare sectors, China has steadily advanced institutional opening-up by aligning its rules, regulations, management and standards with international practices. Diego Ruzzarin, director of Mexico's MPV Media, depicted China as an important source of inspiration for Global South countries over the past four decades, offering valuable experience for their development. As China continues to open up, its unilateral visa-free policies have been extended to more countries, while "China Travel" and "China Shopping" have continued to gain traction as themes online. Ivan Sinichkin, deputy editor-in-chief of Russian newspaper Rossiyskaya Gazeta, said the growing flows of people and goods reflect shared commitment among APEC economies to pursue common development through the opportunities created by Chinese modernization.■

item.title: China's foreign trade maintains rapid growth in first eight months
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-08
BEIJING, Sept. 8 (Xinhua) -- China's foreign trade maintained swift growth in the first eight months of 2026, with both exports and imports posting solid gains, and import growth continuing to outpace exports, official data showed on Tuesday. The country's total goods imports and exports rose 17.6 percent year on year to 34.78 trillion yuan (about 5.13 trillion U.S. dollars) in the January-August period, according to the General Administration of Customs. The growth rate was 0.3 percentage point faster than that recorded in the first seven months of the year. Exports increased 14.6 percent year on year to 20.17 trillion yuan, while imports expanded by 22 percent to 14.61 trillion yuan, the data revealed. In August alone, China's goods trade totaled 4.65 trillion yuan, up 19.8 percent from a year earlier and remaining above the 4-trillion-yuan mark for a sixth consecutive month. Exports grew 18.6 percent year on year in August, while imports rose by 21.7 percent. Both exports and imports registered double-digit growth for a fourth straight month, and import growth exceeded that of exports for a sixth successive month. ■

item.title: China's major river-to-sea canal to open to navigation
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-07
NANNING, Sept. 7 (Xinhua) -- Pinglu Canal in south China's Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region will become operational on Sept. 16, according to a Monday press conference on the canal's opening. The 134.2-km canal links the Xijiang River shipping route in the north with the Beibu Gulf in the south. It is China's first major river-to-sea canal project that has been planned and coordinated at the national level since 1949. Designed to accommodate vessels of up to 5,000 tonnes, the canal stretches along the country's New International Land-Sea Trade Corridor, a strategic route linking China's inland regions with ASEAN and other global markets. It is expected to shorten the shipping distance between China's southwestern hinterland and ASEAN by 560 km and reduce logistics costs by 18 to 30 percent, said Lu Xinning, vice chairperson of the regional government, in another press conference held in early September. "The canal not only overcomes Guangxi's longstanding constraints on river-to-sea connectivity, but will also reshape the economic geography between China and ASEAN," said Lu. Trade between the two sides has seen robust growth in recent years. Data from General Administration of Customs show that bilateral trade between China and ASEAN reached 4.34 trillion yuan (about 640 billion U.S. dollars) in the first half of 2026, up 18.2 percent year on year. The Beibu Gulf Port, a key hub at the southern end of the canal, has become an important gateway for China's opening up to ASEAN. Its container throughput increased from 2.28 million twenty-foot equivalent units (TEU) in 2017 to 10.06 million TEUs in 2025, and the port has established a comprehensive shipping network that covers major ports across ASEAN. ■

Chinese tech giant Huawei on Monday launched the Mate XT 2 tri-fold smartphone powered by the new Kirin 9050 Pro chip, the first high-performance processor to use logic folding technology. The Kirin 9050 Pro stacks logic units in layers within a single chip, shortening signal transmission paths, reducing latency and boosting overall performance, according to a launch event in Guangzhou. The Kirin 9050 Pro stacks logic units in layers within a single chip, shortening signal transmission paths, reducing latency and boosting overall performance, according to a launch event in Guangzhou. The last time Huawei introduced a new Kirin chip at a flagship launch was at the global release of the Mate 40 smartphone six years ago. The strategy appears to be paying off in the market. According to IDC data, Huawei's smartphone shipments grew 19.4 percent year on year in the second quarter of 2026, pushing its market share to 22.6 percent -- the top position in China. item.title: International journalists witness China's rescue efforts in mudslide-ravaged Gyirong
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-07
* A group of journalists from international media outlets, including CNN, Reuters and NBC, visited the mudslide-hit Gyirong Port in southwest China's Xizang Autonomous Region from Saturday to Sunday. The fast-moving chain mudslide, triggered by a high-altitude glacier collapse in Nepal, struck Gyirong Port on Aug. 26. As of 6 p.m. on Sept. 5, 43 people were confirmed dead and 519 remained missing. * At a media briefing by the local emergency rescue headquarters, the journalists heard from technical experts and local officials about ongoing efforts on multiple fronts: the search for the missing, victim identification, community assistance and secondary disaster prevention. * "It's a very difficult condition for the workers, and I very much admired how they keep searching for people," said Brazilian journalist Bruno Falci Bitarelli Medeiros, noting that as global warming is the root cause of the disaster, more concrete actions from the world are needed to prevent these kinds of disasters from happening again. GYIRONG, Xizang, Sept. 7 (Xinhua) -- Even with prior knowledge of the catastrophe, Brazilian journalist Bruno Falci Bitarelli Medeiros was struck by the harsh rescue conditions after a bumpy 12-hour bus ride from Lhasa to the mudslide-hit Gyirong Port in southwest China's Xizang Autonomous Region. The final stretch wound through rugged mountain roads, unpredictable weather and falling rocks. "It's a very difficult condition for the workers, and I very much admired how they keep searching for people," Medeiros said. Medeiros was among a group of journalists from international media outlets including CNN, Reuters and NBC who visited the devastated port from Saturday to Sunday. At a media briefing by the local emergency rescue headquarters, they heard from technical experts and local officials about ongoing efforts on multiple fronts: the search for the missing, victim identification, community assistance and secondary disaster prevention. The fast-moving chain mudslide, triggered by a high-altitude glacier collapse in Nepal, struck Gyirong Port in Xigaze City on the China-Nepal border on Aug. 26. As of 6 p.m. on Sept. 5, 43 people were confirmed dead and 519 remained missing. SEARCH GOING ON At the core disaster zone, a 35-meter-high flood mark, roughly the height of a 12-story building, was scored into the cliff above the ruins. "Everything below the flood mark was originally underwater," said Norbu Tsering, deputy head of the emergency rescue headquarters and acting mayor of Xigaze City. "Power was gone. What you see now is what we've restored in the past couple of days." Land access to the port was restored on the morning of Sept. 2, allowing heavy machinery to move in and clear working areas. Mud deposits average four meters deep in the hardest-hit zone, with some areas reaching 16 meters. Inside the core area, vehicles and machinery are conducting deep-search operations -- excavating, searching and clearing layer by layer during grid-by-grid sweeps. Konda Jagan Mohan Varma from the Press Trust of India watched the operation. "The glacier breakdown brought down a lot of slush, mud and huge rocks together," he said. "A large part of infrastructure was damaged on both sides, in China and Nepal." He noted the scale of the rescue effort unfolding around him -- heavy machinery carving through the debris, teams fanning out across the ruins in methodical searches. Just an hour after the journalists arrived, the valley turned from sunshine to pounding rain, forcing an emergency evacuation. Rescuers have persisted in such conditions for more than 10 days. As of 6 p.m. on Sept. 5, China had deployed over 2,500 rescue personnel, more than 500 vehicle trips and over 9,000 sets of search equipment, and air-dropped more than 5 tonnes of supplies. Two people from a nearby village have been rescued, and nearly 1,000 personal items have been recovered. BEYOND BORDERS After repeated verification, authorities confirmed that 261 foreign nationals from 23 countries, including Nepal, India, Latvia, the United States and Britain, remain missing. For identification, each body is numbered, photographed and sampled for DNA and dental records at the scene. The headquarters has set up a dedicated identification team. So far, none of the bodies retrieved are foreign nationals. Responding to a question about the identification process for the missing, Yang Lahong, deputy director of the foreign affairs office of Xizang, said at the briefing that the names and specific information of missing foreigners have not been made public to protect their privacy, but have been shared with the relevant embassies through diplomatic channels. A 24-hour hotline for families of missing foreign nationals has received 509 calls, with feedback provided promptly, Yang added. At Nepal's request, the Chinese government has dispatched tunnel rescue and DNA testing experts to Nepal, along with emergency material assistance. Through a China-Nepal disaster prevention information notification mechanism, daily updates on meteorology, hydrology, glacial lakes and glaciers are shared with Nepal. After the disaster, many Nepalese border residents were stranded in China due to the port closure. Local authorities have seen to the daily needs of 1,720 Nepalese border residents. Green channels for foreign personnel entry and exit have been opened. A total of 3,388 foreign nationals originally planning to leave via Gyirong Port have been diverted, and authorities have helped 365 Nepalese border residents cross the border to return home. WATCHING FOR NEXT DANGER Preventing secondary disasters remains a priority. More than 170 experts and technicians are now monitoring the area with over 150 sets of equipment, including slope radar and drones. Along the main rescue route, 58 geological hazard spots have been identified, seven of them high-risk. Hu Bo, leader of the China Anneng rescue detection team, serves as a "sentinel" for frontline workers. When upstream data showed abnormal movement, he sounded the retreat signal. Whistles echoed through the gorge as personnel and machinery pulled back to safety zones. Hu said such scenarios can happen several times a night. Muhammad Asghar from the Associated Press of Pakistan observed the monitoring efforts. "The monitoring for secondary disasters is being done tirelessly, day and night," he said. On the site, Medeiros spotted civilian drones flying to observe potential risks for a secondary disaster. "The technology today is being very helpful to rescue operations in this disaster," he said. "Some countries use drones for war, but China uses drones to help people." Medeiros noted that, as global warming is the root cause of the disaster, more concrete actions from the world are needed to prevent these kinds of disasters from happening again, citing China's push for a green economy as an example. Asghar agreed. "Climate change is not the issue of only one country. The whole world should put their heads together," he said. ■
